title: A Kid Sold Me His Lunch for $1 a Day. Years Later, I Learned Why
hook: A kid sold me his lunch for $1… every single day
story: For an entire school year, a kid in my class sold me his lunch for one dollar a day. Every day, same thing. A sandwich, an apple, and a cookie his mom made. I thought I was doing him a favor. He always seemed broke, so I'd hand him my dollar and feel like a good person. What I didn't realize was that I was the one who never had lunch. My dad had lost his job that year, and I'd stopped bringing food without telling anyone. I didn't think anybody noticed. On the last day of school, the kid handed me an envelope and ran off before I could say anything. Inside was every single dollar I'd paid him. One hundred and eighty of them. And a note in messy handwriting. "My mom said you wouldn't take it for free. She said proud people need a way to say yes. Have a good summer." His mom had been packing two lunches every morning. All year. For a kid she'd never even met. I'm a teacher now. And every morning, I keep an extra sandwich in my desk drawer, with a price tag on it that says one dollar… because a kid in my class sold me his lunch for one dollar a day.
